title: Restricting the Brown adjoint along a proper map to $D^b_{ctf}$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible and $p\colon X\to Y$ a proper morphism of standing schemes. Then:

1. the functor $Rp_!\colon\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$ of
   [sk-thm-existence] (2) is isomorphic to the restriction of
   $Rp_*\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$;
2. $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, and the restriction of the right
   adjoint $p^!$ of [sk-thm-existence] (3) to $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ is a right adjoint
   of $Rp_*\colon\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $Y$ separated and of finite type over $k$, so $Y$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. Properness of $p$ includes separatedness and finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the compactification-comparison statements below apply. The factorization $c_0=(X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_X}X\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ is a compactification in [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]: the identity is an open immersion and is quasi-compact because the inverse image of any affine open is that same affine open; its proper part is the given $p$.

source.place: Paragraph (1): the identity compactification; geometric hypotheses made explicit

proof.text:
For the identity open immersion the localization functor in [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] is the identity. Left Kan extension along the identity returns the original presheaf (at each object its defining comma category has that object with its identity as a terminal object), and sheafification of an already given sheaf returns that sheaf. Hence $\mathrm{id}^{\Ab}_!\cong\mathrm{id}$. The same Kan-extension calculation in [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], using the projection $V\times_X X\cong V$, identifies $\mathrm{id}^*_{\Ab}$ with the identity. Write $F=\pi_X^*$ and $R=(\pi_X)_*$. For $h_1=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $h_2=\pi_X$, let $\delta:R\circ(\mathrm{id}_X)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ be the forward pushforward comparison of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. Its fibre-product projection becomes the identity under $V\times_X X\cong V$. The revised definition [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp] makes $c:F\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathrm{id}_X)^*_{\Ab}F$ the conjugate of this forward $\delta$, with the direction reversed by taking mates. To check its component explicitly, use $F\dashv R$ and $(\mathrm{id}_X)^*_{\Ab}\dashv(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$ from [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. Under the Kan-extension identification, the latter is the identity adjunction with identity unit and counit. Thus the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has the same unit $\eta$ as $F\dashv R$. The inverse-mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], with both intervening functors identities, gives
$$c_A=\varepsilon_{F A}\circ F(\eta_A)=\mathrm{id}_{F A},$$
where the first equality also uses $\delta=\mathrm{id}$ under the projection identifications and the second is the triangle identity for $F\dashv R$. Consequently the inverse comparison $c^{-1}:(\mathrm{id}_X)^*_{\Ab}\pi_X^*\to\pi_X^*$ is the identity as well. In the module-object definition [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}}$ is, by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] and [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp], the component of the identity pullback-composition comparison and hence the identity under the identity pullback identification, so restriction of scalars changes nothing. The projection-formula map is the transpose of the unit map specified in [lem-sfb-open-projection-formula]. For the identity localization the Kan-extension unit at $M$ is $\mathrm{id}_M$, so this transpose and its inverse are $\mathrm{id}_{\Lambda_X\otimes M}$ under the identifications above. The action formula of [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] therefore reads $\Lambda_X\otimes M\to M$, the original action. Thus $\mathrm{id}_!\cong\mathrm{id}$ also on module objects, naturally in $M$. Applying this identification in each degree gives $D(\mathrm{id}_!)\cong\mathrm{id}$; the termwise interpretation is precisely [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Consequently the candidate for $c_0$ is $Rp_*D(\mathrm{id}_!)\cong Rp_*$.

source.place: Paragraph (1): identity extension by zero on sheaves, module actions and complexes; compositor direction as corrected in the current reviewed def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp

proof.text: By [det-sf-comp-coherence-single], applied to $c_0$, its ambient candidate $Rp_*D(\mathrm{id}_!)$ restricts to a functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,\Lambda))$. The localizing subcategories, formed with small coproducts in the fixed universe, are closed under isomorphisms by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] (2), so step 2 identifies this functor with the restriction of the ambient $Rp_*$. Let $c$ be the compactification used for $Rp_!$ in [sk-thm-existence] (2). The comparison $\phi_{c_0,c}$ of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle], followed by the identification of step 2, gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:Rp_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*|_{\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))}$. The current single-candidate statement explicitly fixes the positive-characteristic standing field, separated finite-type $k$-schemes and the finite or condensed $\ell$-adic coefficient stages. These hypotheses are exactly the standing setting and admissibility assumed here; its compactification and qcqs hypotheses, and those of the cocycle statement, hold by step 1, and their statements apply to every admissible coefficient stage on the indicated localizing categories. This proves clause (1).

source.place: Paragraph (1): compactification independence on the localizing categories

proof.text: By [sk-thm-existence] (2), $Rp_!K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ whenever $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. The component $\alpha_K$ of step 3 identifies this object with $Rp_*K$. The full subcategory $\Dctf$ is replete by [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], so $Rp_*K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. By [sk-thm-existence] (4), $p^!L\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for every $L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. These two preservation statements make both restrictions into functors on the full subcategories.

source.place: Paragraph (2), first two sentences: preservation and restriction of both functors

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dctf(T,\Lambda))$ for $T=X,Y$, with small coproducts taken in the fixed indexing universe. The current definition [sk-def-localizing-closure] makes $\mathcal T_T$ the full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ on the objects belonging to every full replete triangulated subcategory that contains $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ and is closed under all small ambient coproducts. Each object of $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ belongs to every subcategory in that intersection, hence belongs to $\mathcal T_T$. The fullness asserted by this definition and the fullness of $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude] show that their inclusion is fully faithful: for two $\Dctf$ objects, both Hom sets are the ambient derived Hom set. No derived-completeness condition is imposed on the hull. For $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, the restrictions of step 4 give the bijection
$$
\Hom_{\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)}(Rp_*K,L)
\xrightarrow{\ u\mapsto u\circ\alpha_K\ }
\Hom_{\mathcal T_Y}(Rp_!K,L)
\xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{K,L}\ }
\Hom_{\mathcal T_X}(K,p^!L)
=\Hom_{\Dctf(X,\Lambda)}(K,p^!L),
$$
where $\Phi$ is the adjunction bijection of [sk-thm-existence] (3). Its inverse sends $v$ to $\Phi_{K,L}^{-1}(v)\circ\alpha_K^{-1}$. The first map is natural in $K$ because $\alpha$ is a natural transformation and in $L$ by associativity of composition; the second is natural by the given adjunction. Their composite is therefore the adjunction required in clause (2). Explicitly, if $\eta,\epsilon$ are the unit and counit of $Rp_!\dashv p^!$, the transported unit is $p^!(\alpha_K)\circ\eta_K$ and the transported counit is $\epsilon_L\circ\alpha_{p^!L}^{-1}$. These have source and target in the small full subcategories by step 4. They are the restricted unit and counit after the identification $Rp_!\cong Rp_*$, rather than a literal equality of the two left adjoints.

source.place: Paragraph (2): explicit natural Hom bijection and transported unit/counit; current intersection definition of the localizing hull
